dataset: Primary-source context ledger for photon-limited radial-velocity precision
purpose: These records constrain interpretation. They are not pooled as interchangeable chart points because design goals, formal internal errors, short-term precision, and long-baseline residuals are different estimands.

sources.citation: Bouchy, F., Pepe, F. & Queloz, D. (2001). Fundamental photon noise limit to radial velocity measurements. Astronomy & Astrophysics, 374, 733-739.
sources.role: Defines the optimal spectral-weight and quality-factor formulation used by the controlled experiment.
sources.claim_boundary: A photon-noise lower bound conditioned on a spectrum; not total on-sky precision.

sources.citation: Pepe, F. et al. (2021). ESPRESSO at VLT: On-sky performance and first results. Astronomy & Astrophysics, 645, A96.
sources.reported_context: R=140000 or 190000 in one-UT modes; better than 0.25 m/s during one night and 0.50 m/s over several months, with an instrumental precision compatible with 0.10 m/s.
sources.claim_boundary: Reported on-sky performance under the paper's conditions; not a point on this synthetic model curve.

sources.citation: Petersburg, R. R. et al. (2020). An Extreme-precision Radial-velocity Pipeline: First Radial Velocities from EXPRES. The Astronomical Journal, 159, 187.
sources.reported_context: Median R approximately 137500; formal single-measurement error of 0.3 m/s at per-pixel S/N 250; 51 Peg fit residual RMS of 0.895 m/s.
sources.claim_boundary: Formal error and orbital-fit residual RMS are distinct quantities and are not combined into one benchmark point.

sources.citation: Fischer, D. A. et al. (2016). State of the Field: Extreme Precision Radial Velocities. Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific, 128, 066001.
sources.role: Boundary-of-inference context for calibration, tellurics, detectors, illumination, and photospheric velocities.
sources.claim_boundary: Motivates omitted effects; it does not validate this synthetic spectrum as an instrument forecast.
